body: IPO Apr 2019 at ₹538; first weekly close ₹644 → ATH ₹10,083 (Jun 2026) ≈15.7x (≈19x from the issue price). P/E 26.9 → 58.9 (2.2x) × implied EPS ~7.2x, about 28% rerating. ₹7,550 on 19 Nov 2026 (−25%), P/E ~36. Drawdowns: −45% (COVID 2020), −37% (Dec 2024–Feb 2025). Revenue FY19 ₹7,986 cr → FY26 ₹28,884 cr; OPM 12% → 14%; ROCE 22% → 33%; PAT ₹500 cr → ₹2,708 cr. Early signal (general knowledge, unverified narrative): it listed at a fair ~20–27x as the organised market leader in wires and cables while demand from real-estate, infrastructure, data centres, power transmission and exports accelerated; the FMCG-like distribution of wires and quarterly B2B/export growth were visible in investor decks. The early-2025 drop coincided with reports of a large cement group entering wires and cables, and a Dec 2023 income-tax search hit the stock briefly (both unverified). Lesson: buying a category leader at a reasonable IPO P/E lets EPS do the work. New-entrant headlines cause sharp but survivable drawdowns when ROCE keeps rising.

data.early_signals: leader listed at fair P/E; capex-cycle demand
data.note: Prices: screener.in weekly closes, split/bonus-adjusted. P/E = trailing (TTM); implied EPS x = price multiple / P/E multiple.

title: Polycab 2019–2026: wires & cables leader bought at IPO, ~16x mostly EPS
